new_entities.name: Desiccated thyroid extract
new_entities.description: Porcine-derived desiccated thyroid extract used as thyroid hormone replacement for hypothyroidism.

new_entities.name: Well-being
new_entities.description: Overall subjective well-being, including mood, vitality, symptom burden, and patient-reported health status.

edges.effect_quant: Randomized trials do not show a reliable average well-being advantage for desiccated thyroid extract over levothyroxine, but some patients prefer it. In a 70-patient crossover trial there were no significant symptom or neurocognitive differences despite 49% preferring DTE, and in a later 75-patient three-arm crossover trial overall QoL scores were again similar, though the most symptomatic subgroup improved on T3-containing therapy.
edges.population: adults with primary hypothyroidism who remain interested in alternative replacement strategies despite biochemical control on levothyroxine
edges.mechanism: DTE provides both T4 and proportionally higher T3 than endogenous human thyroid secretion, which may change symptom perception or tissue thyroid hormone exposure in selected patients.
edges.summary: This is a mixed edge rather than a clearly beneficial one. DTE has a persistent niche of patient preference, but controlled trials do not show robust average improvements in well-being across all treated hypothyroid patients.
edges.caveats: DTE has a supraphysiologic T3:T4 ratio relative to normal human thyroid output, and long-term safety data are limited. Apparent benefits may reflect individual responsiveness or preference rather than a consistent class effect on validated quality-of-life outcomes.

evidence.citation: HoangTD et al 2013 J Clin Endocrinol Metab
evidence.notes: Desiccated thyroid extract compared with levothyroxine in the treatment of hypothyroidism: a randomized, double-blind, crossover study.

effect_quant.comparator: preference for DTE (49%) versus levothyroxine (19%) after crossover treatment
